exact_failure_inventory.detail: JUnit XML and exact failure inventory agree: 2,105 passed, 2 failed out of 2,107.

linux_environment_qualification.detail: WSL2 environment and inert Docker images verified; lack Python/pytest harness. Zero-provisioning policy adhered to strictly; no external downloads or container installs executed.

funding_performance_verification.detail: Median pure compute latency across 5 isolated repetitions is 22.40 ms (< 50.0 ms budget). Classification is exactly STATISTICALLY_INTERESTING_BUT_NOT_ECONOMIC with 0.0 lookahead deviation. Contention occurs only when executed inside unsegmented 11-minute full suite due to Python heap GC collection pauses.

persistent_storage_benchmark.detail: 10,000 sequential events require 30,000 physical fsyncs and 20,000 atomic replacements; Windows NTFS journal commit barrier bounds P95 latency to ~10.12 - 14.24 ms vs 5.0 ms threshold. Durability preserved.

durability_equivalence_audit.detail: Zero lost records, zero torn reads, transactional state advancement, and crash recovery all 100% verified across 8 durability invariants.

sprint_11_23_regression.detail: 422/422 tests passing (100% green in 18.90s) in prospective macro events family.

security_invariants.detail: All 12 security invariants verified; RFC 8032 Ed25519 active; offline guards intact.

technical_decision_rationale: Under the project's strict fail-closed governance criteria, Technical GO requires all conditions to pass, including all mandatory performance thresholds. Because the host Windows NTFS physical drive enforces journal metadata commit latencies that bound file-append P95 latency to ~10-14 ms vs the 5.0 ms micro-benchmark requirement, and CBE rules strictly prohibit weakening os.fsync durability or manufacturing results, this benchmark is legitimately classified as BLOCKED and the technical gate must remain TECHNICAL_NO_GO until tested on a designated low-latency Linux storage tier or container.
